title: MAP09 groundwater translation-calibration diagnostic
question: Why does the frozen one-shot MAP09 groundwater translation calibration miss q_gw(href)=q_swap(href) at the 1e-15 m/s gate, and can the local groundwater response at href be measured consistently without changing the bias or G12?

frozen_authority.g12_groundwater_datum_translation: Reuse solve_term_map09 from the repaired G12 test exactly.
frozen_authority.g12_one_shot_bias_rule: For each regime solve q=q_ref with zero bias, then set bias=href-returned_head exactly once.

groundwater_regimes: Reuse all three G12 preregistered groundwater regimes unchanged.

direct_href_inversion.rule: With the frozen one-shot bias, solve fresh constant-flux MODFLOW at the bracket endpoints; require returned heads to bracket href. Perform exactly 20 bisections in imposed q using sign of H(q)-href. The final midpoint q_direct_href is diagnostic only and does not alter the bias.

required_execution_gates: MAP09 href/q/u authority reproduces and E3_MAP href remains available.
All three one-shot G12 biases are reproduced from the unchanged rule.
Every local fixed q probe converges and each centered affine fit has positive slope and max error <=1e-16 m/s.
The fixed direct-q bracket contains href for every regime and all 20 bisection solves complete.
interpretation_rules: G12 remains falsified regardless of G12A outcome.
Compare q_ref-q_at_href and q_ref-q_direct_href; do not relax the G12 1e-15 gate post hoc.
If q_at_href and q_direct_href agree closely while both differ from q_ref, the G12 miss is a one-shot translation-calibration offset rather than affine-fit error.
A later G12B may preregister a local/direct groundwater oracle, but only after G12A is persisted.
